label: Sample Exam Set D
source: ISTQB CTFL v4.0 Sample Exam D, Questions v1.5 / Answers v1.5 (istqb.org)

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical test objective?
o: Finding and fixing defects in the test object
Validating that legal requirements have been met
Building confidence in the quality of the test object
questions.e: Building confidence in the quality of the test object is a typical objective, achieved by tests that pass. Fixing defects is debugging, communication is only a means, and checking legal requirements is verification rather than validation.

questions.q: A designer documents a design for a user interface that does not suitably address disabled users because the designer is tired. The programmer implements the user interface in line with the design but as they are working under severe time pressure, they do not include suitable exception handling in their program code for bonus calculations. When the operational system is used, complaints are made by some disabled users about the interface and the company is subsequently fined by the relevant regulatory authority. No one notices that bonus calculations are sometimes incorrect. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
o: The miscalculation of bonuses is a defect that occasionally occurs
The fine received for failing to address some disabled users is a failure
The programmer working under severe time pressure is a root cause
The design of the user interface includes a designer error
questions.e: The severe time pressure under which the programmer worked is the root cause of the defect. The miscalculation is a failure, the fine is not a failure of the system, and the user interface design contains a design defect caused by the designer's error.

questions.q: Test conditions are being used by testers to generate test cases and execute tests. Even though the test conditions remain the same, the test cases are varied each time. Which of the following 'principles of testing' is being addressed through the variation of test cases?
o: Early testing saves time and money
questions.e: Varying the tests generated from the same test conditions keeps them from becoming stale, which addresses the 'tests wear out' principle. The other principles concern user satisfaction, early defect removal and defect distribution.

questions.q:
Match the test tasks (1-4) with the test activities (A-D):
1. Derive test cases from test conditions
2. Identify reusable testware
3. Organize test cases into test procedures
4. Evaluate the test basis and the test object
A. Test analysis
B. Test design
C. Test implementation
D. Test completion
questions.e: Deriving test cases from test conditions is test design (1B), identifying reusable testware is test completion (2D), organizing test cases into procedures is test implementation (3C), and evaluating the test basis and object is test analysis (4A).

questions.q:
Which of the following testware is produced as a result of performing test implementation?
i. Test completion report
ii. Data held in a database used for test inputs and expected results
iii. The list of elements needed to build the test environment
iv. Documented sequences of test cases in execution order
v. Test cases
questions.e: Test implementation produces test procedures (iv) and test data (ii), along with scripts, suites, schedules and environment elements. The completion report is from test completion, environment requirements and test cases come from test design.

questions.q: Which of the following is MOST likely to describe a task performed by someone in a test management role?
o: Evaluate the test basis and the test object
Assess testability of the test object
questions.e: The test management role covers test planning, monitoring and control, and test completion, so creating the test completion report belongs to it. The other three tasks belong to the testing role as part of analysis and design.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of the whole team approach?
o: Faster deployment of deliverables to the end users
Reduced collaboration with external business users
questions.e: The whole team approach promotes communication, collaboration and collective accountability, while every member stays individually accountable for quality. It does not guarantee faster deployment and it increases collaboration with business representatives.

questions.q:
Which of the following are MOST likely to be considered benefits of the independence of testing?
i. The testers work in a different location from the developers
ii. Testers question the assumptions programmers make while writing code
iii. A confrontational dynamic has been established between testers and developers
iv. Developers have convinced themselves that testers are mostly accountable for quality
v. Testers have different biases than those held by the developers
questions.e: Questioning the assumptions behind the code (ii) and bringing different biases and viewpoints (v) are the benefits of independence. Separation, confrontation and developers feeling less accountable are disadvantages.

questions.q: Which of the following is a good testing practice that applies to all software development lifecycles?
o: Each test level has specific and distinct test objectives
Test implementation and execution for a given test level should start during the corresponding development phase
Testers should start test design as soon as drafts of the relevant work products become available
Every dynamic testing activity has a corresponding static testing activity
questions.e: Each test level tests a different test object and should have its own distinct objectives, otherwise work is duplicated. Test analysis and design start early but implementation and execution come later, test design needs an agreed basis rather than a draft, and static and dynamic testing do not map one to one.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a test-first approach to development?
questions.e: Behavior-Driven Development is a well-known test-first approach, as are TDD and ATDD. The other three names do not describe test-first practices.

questions.q: Which of the following is MOST likely to be a challenge encountered when implementing DevOps?
o: Making sure that non-functional quality characteristics are not overlooked
The need for more manual testers with suitable experience
Setting up the test automation as part of the delivery pipeline
questions.e: Introducing DevOps requires defining and setting up the delivery pipeline, adopting and maintaining CI/CD tools and establishing test automation, which is a genuine challenge. DevOps raises the visibility of non-functional characteristics, stabilises environments and reduces manual testing.

questions.q: Which of the following BEST describes retrospectives?
o: Retrospectives allow team members to identify other team members who did not fully contribute to achieving quality as required by the whole team approach
Retrospectives give testers an opportunity to identify activities that were successful so that these are retained when potential improvements are made in the future
Retrospectives are where agile team members are allowed to voice their concerns about management and customers in a blameless environment
Retrospectives give agile team members a forum where they focus on discussing the plan and technical decisions for the next iteration
questions.e: A retrospective discusses what went well so that it is kept, and what could improve and how, at the end of an iteration. It is not a meeting to blame individuals, vent about customers, or plan the next iteration.

questions.q: Which of the following tests is MOST likely to be performed as part of functional testing?
o: The test checks that the sort function puts the elements of the list or array in ascending order
The test checks whether the sort function completes sorting within one second of starting
The test checks how easily the sort function can be changed from sorting ascending to sorting descending
The test checks that the sort function still functions correctly when moved from a 32-bit to a 64-bit architecture
questions.e: Checking that elements are sorted ascending tests functional correctness, which is functional testing. The others test performance efficiency, modifiability and adaptability, which are non-functional characteristics.

questions.q: Which of the following is MOST likely to be a trigger that leads to maintenance testing of a currency exchange system?
o: The developers reported that changing the currency exchange system was difficult and the testers decided to check if this was true
The refund option of the currency exchange system was removed as it did not always repay the correct amount to customers
The agile team has started developing a user story that adds a new customer loyalty feature to the currency exchange system
The language support option of the currency exchange system was used to enable both English and local language currency transactions
questions.e: Removing the faulty refund option is a modification of the system, which is one of the triggers for maintenance testing. Testing modifiability, a new feature and a configuration option are not maintenance testing triggers.

questions.q: Which of the following CANNOT be examined by static testing?
questions.e: Static testing examines work products that humans or tools can interpret. Encrypted code is too complex for human interpretation and, when properly encrypted, cannot be analysed by tools, so it cannot be examined statically.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the value of static testing is CORRECT?
o: The defect types found by static testing are different from the defect types that can be found by dynamic testing
Dynamic testing can detect the defect types that can be found by static testing plus some additional defect types
Dynamic testing can identify some of the defects that can be found by static testing but not all of them
Static testing can identify the defect types that can be found by dynamic testing as well as some extra defect types
questions.e: Some defects are only findable statically (unreachable code, defects in non-executable work products), some by both, and some only dynamically (performance and memory problems). So dynamic testing catches some but not all of the static defect types.

questions.q:
What is the CORRECT sequence of review activities for these descriptions?
1. Detected anomalies are deliberated upon, and determinations are reached regarding their status, ownership, and any further steps needed
2. Defects are recorded, and any needed updates are addressed prior to the acceptance of the work product
3. Reviewers employ techniques to come up with suggestions and questions about the work product and to spot anomalies
4. The objective of the review and its schedule are established to ensure a focused and efficient review
5. Participants are provided with access to the item being reviewed
questions.e: The generic review process runs planning (4), review initiation (5), individual review (3), communication and analysis (1), then fixing and reporting (2).

questions.q: Which participant in the review process is responsible for ensuring that the review meetings run effectively and that everyone at the meetings can voice their opinions freely?
questions.e: The moderator, also called the facilitator, manages time, mediates discussions and creates a safe environment for everyone. The manager decides what is reviewed, the review leader oversees the whole review, and chairperson is not a review role.

questions.q: You perform system testing of an e-commerce web application and are given the requirement: 'REQ 05-017. If the total cost of purchases exceeds $100, the customer gets a 5% discount on subsequent purchases. Otherwise, the customer does not receive a discount.' Which test techniques will be MOST helpful in designing test cases based on this requirement?
questions.e: The requirement specifies the desired behaviour and contains a clear boundary ('exceeds $100'), so black-box techniques such as boundary value analysis and decision table testing fit best. White-box techniques need the code or design, and risk-based techniques are not a test technique type.

questions.q:
A cinema ticket system calculates the discount from the client's birth year (BY) and the current year (CY), where D = CY - BY: if D < 0 print 'birth year cannot be greater than current year'; if 0 <= D < 18 apply the student discount; if 18 <= D < 65 apply no discount; if D >= 65 apply the pensioner discount.
Your suite already has: BY 1990, CY 2020 (no discount) and BY 2030, CY 2029 (error message). Which of the following test data sets should be added to achieve full valid equivalence partitioning coverage for the discount type?
questions.e: The missing partitions are the student discount and the pensioner discount. Option b gives D = 65 (pensioner) and option e gives D = 0 (student). Option a gives D = 64 and option d gives D = 18, both no discount, and option c gives a negative D, the error partition already covered.

questions.q: You test a temperature control system for a cold storage facility. The input is the temperature in full degrees Celsius. If the temperature is between 0 and 2 degrees inclusive the system displays 'temperature OK', for lower temperatures 'temperature too low' and for higher temperatures 'temperature too high'. Using two-value boundary value analysis, which set of test inputs provides the highest level of boundary value coverage?
questions.e: The boundary values are -1, 0, 2 and 3. Option c covers all four, while a and b each cover only two and d covers none of them exactly, because -2 and 4 are boundaries of the extended partitions rather than the -1 to 3 boundaries in question.

questions.q:
A decision table has seven rules (R1-R7):
R1: age 0-18, unregistered -> category A
R2: age 19-65, 0-4 years experience, unregistered -> category A
R3: age 19-65, more than 4 years experience, unregistered -> category B
R4: age above 65, unregistered -> category B
R5: age 0-18, registered -> category B
R6: age 19-65, registered -> category D
R7: age above 65, registered -> category C
Existing test cases cover R2, R3, R6 and R7. Which test case, when added, will increase the decision table coverage?
o: 66-year-old, unregistered man with no experience; expected result: category B
55-year-old, unregistered woman with 2 years of experience; expected result: category A
19-year-old, registered woman with 5 years of experience; expected result: category D
No additional test case can increase the already achieved decision table coverage
questions.e: The 66-year-old unregistered case matches R4, which is not yet covered. Options b and c repeat R2 and R6, and four of the seven rules are covered before the addition, so coverage can still grow.

questions.q: You apply state transition testing to a hotel room reservation system with 4 states (Requesting, Confirmed, Waiting list, End) and 5 events (Available, NotAvailable, ChangeRoom, Cancel, Pay). The valid transitions are: Requesting -Available-> Confirmed; Requesting -NotAvailable-> Waiting list; Confirmed -ChangeRoom-> Requesting; Waiting list -Available-> Confirmed; Confirmed -Cancel-> End; Waiting list -Cancel-> End; Confirmed -Pay-> End. All test cases start in Requesting. Which test case, as a sequence of events, achieves the highest valid transitions coverage?
questions.e: Option b exercises Requesting to Confirmed, Confirmed to Requesting, Requesting to Waiting list, Waiting list to Confirmed and Confirmed to End: five of the seven valid transitions. Option a covers four, option c three, and option d is infeasible because nothing follows Cancel from the End state.

questions.q: Your test suite S for a program P achieves 100% statement coverage. It consists of three test cases, each of which achieves 50% statement coverage. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
o: Executing S will cause all possible failures in P
S achieves 100% branch coverage for P
Every executable statement in P containing a defect has been run at least once during the execution of S
After removing one test case from S, the remaining two test cases will still achieve 100% statement coverage
questions.e: Full statement coverage means every executable statement, including defective ones, ran at least once. A defective statement may still not fail, statement coverage does not imply branch coverage, and each test case may cover statements the others do not.

questions.q: Why does white-box testing facilitate defect detection even when the software specification is vague, outdated or incomplete?
o: Test cases are designed based on the structure of the test object rather than the specification
For each white-box test technique the coverage can be well-defined and easily measured
White-box test techniques are very well designed to detect omissions in the requirements
White-box test techniques can be used in both static testing and dynamic testing
questions.e: White-box techniques ignore the specification and work from the implementation, so they still produce tests when the specification is poor and can reveal extra or hidden code. They cannot detect requirements omissions, and measurability is not the reason.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT anticipated by the tester while applying error guessing?
o: The developer misunderstood the formula in the user story for calculating the interest
The developer wrote 'FA = A*(1+IR^N)' instead of 'FA = A*(1+IR)^N' in the source code
The developer missed the seminar on new compound interest rate legislation
The accuracy of the interest calculated by the system is not precise enough
questions.e: Error guessing anticipates errors, defects and failures. Missing a seminar is a root cause behind a possible error, and root causes are not what the technique predicts.

questions.q: Which of the following is true about exploratory testing?
o: Test cases are designed before the exploratory testing session starts
The tester can perform test execution, but cannot perform test design
Exploratory testing results are good predictors of the number of remaining defects
During exploratory testing the tester may use black-box test techniques
questions.e: In exploratory testing the tester designs, executes and evaluates simultaneously and may apply any useful technique, including black-box ones. Test cases are created during the session and the results depend on the tester, so they are not a reliable predictor of remaining defects.

questions.q: Which collaborative user story writing practice enables the team to achieve a collective understanding of what needs to be delivered?
o: Planning poker, so that a team can achieve consensus on the effort needed to implement a user story
Reviews, so that a team can detect inconsistencies and contradictions in a user story
Iteration planning, so that user stories with the highest business value for a customer can be prioritized for implementation
Conversation, so that team members can understand how the software will be used
questions.e: In the three Cs of user stories, conversation is the practice that explains how the software will be used and lets the team agree meaningful acceptance criteria and a shared vision.

questions.q:
You design test cases for the user story: As a customer, I want to be able to filter search results by price range, so that I can find products within my budget more easily. Acceptance criteria: 1. the filter should work for all versions of the application from version 3.0 upwards; 2. the filter should allow the customer to set a price range with a minimum and a maximum price; 3. the search results should update dynamically as the customer adjusts the price range filter. Precondition in all test cases: only two products exist, A at $100 and B at $110.
Which of the following is the BEST example of a test case for this user story?
o: Enter the webpage and set the filter to show prices between $90 and $100. Expected: results show product A only. Set the maximum price to $110. Expected: results now include both products A and B

Enter the webpage. Expected: the default minimum and maximum prices are $100 and $110 respectively. Add product C to stock with price $120. Refresh the client's webpage. Expected: the default maximum price changes to $120

Enter the webpage and set the filter to show prices between $90 and $115. Expected: results show both products A and B. Change currency from USD to EUR. Expected: the filter range changes correctly to EUR values, according to the current exchange rate

Enter the webpage with three different browsers: Edge, Chrome and Opera. In each browser set the filter between $90 and $110. Expected: results include both products A and B and the results layout is the same in all three browsers
questions.e: Option a tests acceptance criteria 2 and 3 by setting a price range and checking that results update dynamically. The others test defaults, currency conversion and browser compatibility, none of which the acceptance criteria describe.

questions.q: Which of the following BEST define EXIT criteria in a testing project?
o: Test cases achieved at least 80% statement coverage
All test analysts are ISTQB certified at the Foundation Level
questions.e: Running out of budget and reaching a coverage target both mark the end of testing, so they are exit criteria. Budget approval, availability of the test basis and certified analysts are conditions checked before testing starts.

questions.q: The team wants to estimate the time needed for one tester to execute four test cases for a software component. Measures for a single test case: best case 1 hour, most likely 3 hours, worst case 8 hours. Using the three-point estimation technique, what is the final estimate of the time needed to execute all four test cases?
questions.e: E = (a + 4m + b) / 6 = (1 + 12 + 8) / 6 = 3.5 hours per test case, so four test cases need 3.5 x 4 = 14 hours.

questions.q:
A traceability matrix shows which test cases cover which requirements: TC1 covers Req1, Req3, Req4 and Req7; TC2 covers Req1, Req3 and Req4; TC3 covers Req5 and Req6; TC4 covers Req2.
You want to prioritize the test cases using the additional coverage prioritization technique and execute all four. Which test case should be executed LAST?
questions.e: TC1 covers the most requirements first. TC3 then adds Req5 and Req6, TC4 adds the last uncovered requirement Req2, so TC2 adds nothing new and runs last.

questions.q: How can the testing quadrants be beneficial for testing?
o: They help in test planning by dividing the test process into four phases, corresponding to the four basic test levels: component, integration, system, and acceptance testing
They help in assessing the high-level coverage (e.g., requirements coverage) based on low-level coverage (e.g., code coverage)
They help non-technical stakeholders to understand the different test types and that some test types are more relevant to certain test levels than others
They help agile teams to develop a communication strategy based on classifying people according to four basic psychological types, and on modelling the relations between them
questions.e: The quadrants relate test types to whether they are business or technology facing and whether they support the team or critique the product, which helps stakeholders understand the testing picture. They are not a phase model, a coverage model or a psychological model.

questions.q: For a given risk, its risk level is $1,000 and its risk likelihood is estimated as 50%. What is the risk impact?
questions.e: In quantitative risk analysis risk level = likelihood x impact, so impact = 1,000 / 0.5 = $2,000.

questions.q: Which of the following are product risks?
questions.e: Poor architecture and too long response time concern characteristics of the product itself. Scope creep, cost-cutting and poor tool support are project risks about managing the work.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid purpose for a test report?
o: Tracking test progress and identifying areas that require further attention
Providing information on the tests executed, their results, and defects found
Providing information about each defect, such as the steps to reproduce it
Providing information on testing planned for the next period
questions.e: Reporting the details of a single defect, such as reproduction steps, is the purpose of a defect report. Progress, results and planned testing are all valid purposes of a test report.

questions.q: A user reported a software failure. A support engineer asked for the software version number where the failure was observed. Based on that version number the team reassembled all the files that made up the release, which let a developer analyse, find and fix the defect. Which of the following enabled this?
questions.e: Configuration management identifies, controls and tracks work products and records the items of each baseline, so a previous baseline can be reproduced. Risk management, monitoring and the whole team approach do not track configuration items.

questions.q:
A defect report for a Book Lending System states: unable to return a book; severity high; environment Windows 10, Google Chrome; when attempting to return a book the system does not register the return and the book remains checked out; steps: log in as a user who has checked out a book, click Book Return for that book; expected: the book is returned and no longer appears as checked out; actual: the book remains checked out and is not registered as returned; attachments: empty.
Which of the following is MOST likely to help the developer reproduce the failure quickly?
o: Adding information about which users and which books the failure affects to the Description section
Filling in the missing value for the Priority field
Adding memory dumps and database snapshots taken after each step described in the Steps to Reproduce section to the Attachments section
Repeating the same test case for different environments and writing defect reports for each of them separately
questions.e: Naming the users and books involved gives the developer the concrete input data needed to reproduce the failure. Priority does not aid reproduction, and adding every dump and snapshot makes the report unusable.

questions.q:
Which of the following test tool categories are MOST likely to facilitate test execution?
i. Collaboration tools
ii. DevOps tools
iii. Management tools
iv. Non-functional testing tools
v. Test design and implementation tools
questions.e: DevOps tools run the delivery pipeline and CI/CD including component tests, and non-functional testing tools execute tests that are hard or impossible to do by hand. Collaboration, management and design tools generate or organise testware rather than execute it.

questions.q: Which of the following is MOST likely to be a risk of test automation?
o: The detection of additional high-severity defects
Providing measures that are too complicated for humans to derive
questions.e: If the automation is incompatible with the development platform it cannot pass inputs to the test object or receive results from it. The other three items are benefits of test automation.
